_comment: Team Tether rank palettes (spec sec36), on top of NP1's palette and accessory mechanisms. CLAUDE.md/D24: human NPCs reuse the trainer, Grandpa and Warden rigs, never a new mesh. NP4's Team Tether Grunt base exists (assets_raw/grunt/textured/model.glb) but has no path into the game yet -- NP4-rig (area: art, lane: art) has to rig/animate/install it first. Until then the only faction-appropriate rig actually installed is the Warden's, so every rank below reuses his geometry.
_comment_single_material: All three of today's human rigs carry exactly one fused material (character_model.gd's own _apply_palette comment), and that material's emission channel (a full-white self-lit copy of the same painted texture, fixed alongside this item so palette tints are visible at all -- see character_model.gd's _shared_variant_material) means a body-only palette can shift how BRIGHT the same outfit reads, never a genuinely different colour family. A first pass using body brightness alone (grunt darkest, warden full original) did not survive blind review: it read as a lighting gradient, not a rank system -- 'someone duplicated a mesh four times and nudged an exposure value.'
_comment_badge: So the real rank marker is a chest badge (NP1's existing 'accessories' mechanism -- a placeholder primitive on its own material, independent of the body palette, per CLAUDE.md's Prototyping section) that escalates in BOTH colour and size: plain grey and small for the grunt, up through bronze, brass and the Warden's own largest, richest gold. The body brightness ladder stays as a secondary cue underneath it, not the primary one.

warden.label: Warden
warden._comment: No palette override -- his own board-06 painted finish is already the richest tier. Only the badge is added, at the top of the same escalating language the other three use. Round-2 blind review: gold-on-gold made captain and Warden collapse into the same badge at a glance ('the color plateau between rank 3 and rank 4'). Shifted the Warden's own badge to a red/crimson family instead of a brighter gold -- data/config/palette.json's tether_oxblood is reserved for exactly this ('Team Tether banners, equipment and uniforms, never on friendly or neutral elements'), and the Warden IS the top of that same faction, so a red accent both solves the collision and uses the project's own reserved colour correctly rather than inventing an unrelated one.

_comment_scale: Every human rig (trainer/Grandpa/Warden) sits under an Armature node with a flat 0.01 scale -- HANDOFF.md sec6's 'centimetre-unit skeleton under a 0.01 Armature node with x100 inverse binds', the same bug that produced the giant-player fit issue. character_model.gd's _attach_part() sets a placeholder's `position` as a LOCAL child of a BoneAttachment3D inside that scaled chain, so both `offset` and `size` below are in that same shrunk local space, not real metres: a size of 13.0 here renders as a 0.13m sphere in the actual game world, and an offset of 30 along one axis moves it 0.30m in world space. Measured directly (offset [30,0,0]/[0,30,0]/[0,0,30] each moved the attached part almost exactly 0.30m along the matching WORLD axis with no rotation to account for), not guessed -- confirmed the shared _attach_part() mechanism NP1's hair also uses has this same scale, so hair's own tiny offset (0.08) is likely rendering at ~0.0008m, effectively invisible too. Left untouched here rather than fixed for everyone: changing hair's placement is a real, currently-unverified visual change outside NP2's scope, not a call to make inside this item.
_comment_badge_scale: Badge sizes and offsets are METRES, and were authored 100x too large -- size 7.0 to 16.0 with an offset of [0,30,25]. character_model.gd's own default (`acc.get("size", 0.12)`) is the giveaway: 12cm is what a chest badge should be. Applied as metres, the grunt wore a 3.5m-RADIUS sphere thirty metres above his own head, and the ladder made it worse with rank -- the Warden's was 8m. The owner saw them from across the valley and asked what the balls on the stronghold were. Divided by 100 here, which preserves the intended escalation exactly (7cm grunt -> 16cm warden) and puts the badge on the chest.
